context:
Answered in chat, 14:55 CDT: (a), with a condition. In your words: "shivinate7 should be the default unless if it's a repo that shivinate7 doesn't have access too of course". So the PC's default login is shivinate7, and a repo that shivinate7 cannot reach uses ssemwal-cdc. Filed to step gh-account-clear; the ruling lands in a decision record on main when that lane builds it.

Goal: every gh command you paste runs as the login you expect, with no surprise.
Problem (risk): your PC holds two gh logins, and the active one decides what a pasted command can change; only you pick the default.
Based on (measured): gh auth switch printed the active login at 14:52 CDT; the PC is now on shivinate7.
Based on (read): decision main-branch-protection says protection writes need admin, and ssemwal-cdc has push, not admin.

options.how: Leave the PC on shivinate7. Admin steps, such as a protection switch, run with no switch first.
options.label: shivinate7, the repo owner
options.lose: Every pasted command runs with admin rights, so a wrong command can change settings or protection.

options.gain: Day-to-day commands cannot change settings or protection.
options.how: Switch the PC back to ssemwal-cdc. An admin step starts with gh auth switch to shivinate7 and switches back at the end.
options.label: ssemwal-cdc, the work login
options.lose: Admin steps carry two more lines, and a step that forgets the switch back leaves admin active.

ref: gh-account-clear (owner gh steps name their account); waiting item 101 (protection switch)
title: Which GitHub login stays active on your PC?
why: Owner commands work with no switch, and step gh-account-clear makes each step name the login it needs anyway (coordinator's chat pick, 14:54 CDT).
